title: Contractor Estimate, Quote and Job-Cost Control Workbook
description: A jurisdiction-aware estimating and job-cost workbook for small contractors, created as the first Risk B pilot for the STRUCTURA AI Production Factory.

requirements.description: Create estimates from categorised labour, material, plant, subcontract and allowance cost lines.
Calculate and clearly distinguish cost markup from sales margin.
Convert an accepted quotation into an original controlled job budget without re-entry.
Track budget, commitments, actual costs, forecast final cost and forecast profit without double counting.
Track approved and pending variations or change orders separately from the original contract.
Support configurable VAT, sales-tax or GST treatment without embedding time-sensitive tax advice.
Provide a print-ready quotation and a management dashboard with visible assumptions and warnings.
Protect calculated cells while keeping formulas auditable and all intended inputs clearly identified.

source_register.title: STRUCTURA template-market prioritisation decision
source_register.location: Project issue and product-evidence pack to be committed before SPECIFIED

test_register.description: Verify category and total calculations over empty, ordinary and boundary-value cost lines.
Verify markup and margin against independently calculated known-answer cases.
Verify quotation-to-budget conversion preserves the approved baseline and audit trail.
Verify commitment, actual, forecast and profit reconciliation without duplicate costs.
Verify pending and approved changes affect contract value and forecasts correctly.
Verify configurable tax calculations, rounding and tax-exclusive or inclusive presentation.
Verify dashboard reconciliation and print rendering in supported Excel environments.
Verify protected cells, editable inputs, formula visibility and error messages.

known_limitations: This EVIDENCED manifest is not a sellable or approved workbook release.
Tax percentages, labour rates, prices and legal wording must be supplied and verified by the user for the applicable jurisdiction.
The product provides commercial decision support and is not accounting, tax, legal or financial advice.
Google Sheets parity is not committed until compatibility acceptance criteria are approved during specification.
